item.title: Texans claim Nikko Remigio, release Dare Ogunbowale
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Texans have made a couple of roster moves on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
The Texans have made a couple of roster moves on Friday.

Houston announced the team has claimed receiver/returner Nikko Remigio off of waivers.

The Chiefs let Remigio go earlier this week.

In his fourth season, Remigio averaged 26.5 yards per kick return and 5.6 yards per punt return this season for Kansas City.

As a corresponding move, the Texans have released running back Dare Ogunbowale, who is subject to waivers now that the trading deadline has passed.

item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Officially, Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St.
item.content:encoded:
Officially, Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown is questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots in Germany with a rib injury. Unofficially, it is extraordinarily unlikely that St. Brown would miss this game.

St. Brown has always been more than willing to play through injuries, and this game means a lot to him because his mother is German, he speaks fluent German, and he has been circling this game on his calendar as an important one for him personally.

Three Lions have been ruled out: safety Kerby Joseph, center Cade Mays and cornerback DJ Reed. Joining St. Brown as questionable is running back Sione Vaki.

Other Lions dealing with injuries this week are quarterback Jared Goff, safety Brian Branch, running back Jacob Saylors and pass rusher DJ Wonnum, but they all practiced in full the last two days and will be good to go on Sunday.

item.title: Aaron Glenn expects Garrett Wilson to clear concussion protocol, play vs. Bills
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: It sounds like Jets receiver Garrett Wilson is on track to return to action on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
It sounds like Jets receiver Garrett Wilson is on track to return to action on Sunday.

Head coach Aaron Glenn said that Wilson has just one more step of concussion protocol to clear and he's confident the wideout will do so.

"I see that happening," Glenn said.

Wilson missed last week's game while in the protocol. He has caught 43 passes for 527 yards with three touchdowns so far this year.

Glenn noted that everyone else aside from linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) is expected to practice in full on Friday.

That includes rookie receiver Omar Cooper, who has been listed as limited on the first two injury reports of the week with an ankle issue.

New York’s final injury report of the week with game statuses is due out later on Friday.

item.title: Cam Skattebo stayed in his stance instead of pushing Jameis Winston's tush on key play
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Giants running back Cam Skattebo stayed in his stance and didn't participate in the play on a key short-yardage snap late in the Giants' loss on Thursday night.
item.content:encoded:
Giants running back Cam Skattebo stayed in his stance and didn't participate in the play on a key short-yardage snap late in the Giants' loss on Thursday night.

With the Giants leading 21-17 and 3:56 remaining in the fourth quarter on Thursday night, they faced a third-and-1 and sent Jameis Winston in for a quarterback sneak. A first down would have given the Giants a great chance at a long, clock-draining drive. Instead they were stopped, punted, and ended up losing.

As Winston plowed into the line, Skattebo was behind him and could have run in to try to push him forward to gain a yard. Instead, Skattebo stayed in his stance, and by the time he actually got involved in the play, the Commanders had stopped Winston's forward progress.

It's unclear why Skattebo didn't do anything, and he wasn't asked about it after the game. But at a time when every team in the league is well aware of the value of teammates pushing the quarterback forward on sneaks, it was a bizarre play, and one that proved costly for the Giants.

item.title: New Jags Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates will sit out Sunday's game vs. Titans
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Two of Jacksonville's deadline acquisitions will not be on the field for the club this weekend.
item.content:encoded:
Two of Jacksonville's deadline acquisitions will not be on the field for the club this weekend.

Jaguars head coach Liam Coen told reporters in his Friday press conference that safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackle Jordan Davis will sit out Sunday's matchup against the Titans because they did not have a bye week with their previous teams. Davon Godchaux, who did have a bye, is set to play.

"Want to be able to make sure [that with] player safety, putting them in a position to succeed, also learn the system, and just give those guys a week to be able to do that," Coen said.

Coen added that the club had been talking about doing that this week and made the final decision to rest the players on Friday.

The head coach has been impressed with all of the acquisitions so far.

"Yeah, I mean, Jesse Bates has been here until about 10:30 every night, which has been pretty cool seeing him in there learning, grinding, working through it," Coen said. "There’s obviously so much that safeties have to be able to communicate and operate with in the backend of the entire structure. I’ve really appreciated the way him, Jordan, and Davon have all gone through the work week. Obviously, Davon and Jesse have been through different organizations, teams, moves — this is new for Jordan. And he’s worked his tail off with the strength and conditioning and sports science, athletic training guys this week. And he’s putting his best foot forward to hopefully be able to get out next week for us."

The Jaguars will be on the road to face the Giants in Week 11, where Davis and Bates will make their respective debuts.

item.title: Troy Aikman engages in potential pre-tampering with Kyle Shanahan
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: If Troy Aikman exits broadcasting after this season (last month, he put the chance at "50-50") and if Aikman lands a key position in a front office, the name at the top of his head-coaching wishlist will already be known.
item.content:encoded:
If Troy Aikman exits broadcasting after this season (last month, he put the chance at "50-50") and if Aikman lands a key position in a front office, the name at the top of his head-coaching wishlist will already be known.

Via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing, Aikman said during a Thursday appearance on 96.7 The Ticket in Dallas that, if he were running an NFL team, he would try to hire 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan.

“I’ve been asked a lot of questions here, certainly over the last several weeks, about any aspirations that I may have of going in a front office,” Aikman said. “Or ‘Who would you hire as your head coach?’ If I was in a position to hire someone as a head coach, [the] first call I’d make is to the 49ers and say, ‘How much is it going to take to get Kyle Shanahan? Because I think he’s that good. And yes, I’ve always believed this, but coaching matters and it has an impact on an organization.”

It's not tampering because Aikman currently isn't running a team. (It could technically be "tampering light" if he's still working for the Dolphins.) And the information gives Shanahan plenty of leverage in his dealings with the 49ers, if Aikman joins the likes of Matt Millen, John Lynch, and John Elway as former players with little or no front-office experience who find themselves working in high-level jobs with a team.

Aikman has previously made similar comments about Shanahan, in the context of the Bears' latest coaching vacancy.

“There has been discussion about, ‘Do you give up some picks and see if you can maybe make a deal for a guy like Kyle Shanahan?’" Aikman said during a game in 2024. "I would be all in on that. Because he would develop a quarterback, and he’s a hell of a head coach. But can you pull that off? That’s a better question. And who might you hire that has no head-coaching experience as an offensive guy? You never know the answer to that, as to how good they’re gonna be.”

While it seems to be working out pretty well for the Bears and their head coach who had no head-coaching experience, the point remains that Aikman would try to hire Shanahan, if Aikman is ever in a position to hire a coach.

And there's one last twist to this story that currently isn't known. When Aikman was consulting with the Dolphins during their latest search for a G.M. and head coach, did Aikman advise Miami to call about Shanahan? If so, did they?

Shanahan is in his 10th season with the 49ers. He's taken the team to two Super Bowls. Barring the franchise's first championship since 1994 (which could come this year), there could be a point where Shanahan reaches an Andy Reid-style mutual expiration date.

If that ever happens, Shanahan will have options. Especially if Aikman ends up getting hired to be someone's G.M.

item.title: Justin Jefferson: It's a joy to see Kirk Cousins take over as a leader
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Kirk Cousins is back in Minnesota, and perhaps no one is more excited about that than Justin Jefferson.
item.content:encoded:
Kirk Cousins is back in Minnesota, and perhaps no one is more excited about that than Justin Jefferson.

The wide receiver had career highs in catches (128) and yards (1,809) and earned the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year award in Cousins' last full season with the Vikings in 2022.

Jefferson, though, said he has "no expectations."

"It's really just going out there and just executing our plays," Jefferson said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN. "It's not really getting too juiced up about him being here or anybody being back there. It's just all about understanding the plays that are being called, understanding the jobs that we have and executing our responsibilities. And just the plays that are there, and the plays that could be made, we just need to continue to just make those type of plays. And I'm pretty sure that the results would be a lot better.

"He just understands the game. He's a guy that studies the game a lot. He understands how the defenses play, especially covering me. And he understands, the plays that we have called that are kind of my plays and he understands the timing and the windows to throw those type of plays, but he also doesn't force those type of plays to me and he just lets the game come to me."

Jefferson said it was "a joy to hear [Cousins] just take over and be a leader in the meeting room, on the field."

"He's being vocal," Jefferson said. "Just making sure that everybody hears the plays that he's talking about and the notes that he has for certain routes, certain plays. And he's just making sure that everybody's on the same page. So it's definitely cool to hear that type of leadership and command. If you know Kirk, that's pretty normal from him. So it's definitely kind of cool him being back in that room and him taking that control."

item.title: Chiefs STs coordinator Dave Toub: We're confident Harrison Butker will come through it
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Chiefs have had a kicking problem for a while.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs have had a kicking problem for a while.

But at least this week, they're still sticking with Harrison Butker.

Butker While Butker was one of the league’s most accurate kickers for years, that has not been the case over the last few seasons. He’s now missed 17 kicks since the start of last year, which is a league-high.

Butker’s struggles led the Chiefs to sign former Ravens kicker Justin Tucker to the practice squad. But to this point, Kansas City hasn’t used Tucker in a game.

This week, special teams coordinator Dave Toub once again told reporters why the club is sticking with Butker.

“We're going to keep pounding it,” Toub said, via transcript from the team. "We're going to keep working it and keep kicking him.

“He's going to come through it. I mean, we're confident that he will. We're just going to keep practicing him and keep working on little things, and he's looked good in practice. There's a reason why he's still our kicker.”

Butker has made 12-of-19 field goals and 22-of-23 extra points so far in 2026.

item.content:encoded:
A reality TV series is once again pulling from the NFL well.

ABC announced on Friday that Commanders practice squad quarterback Sam Hartman is The Bachelor for the next season of the show, which will premiere on March 21.

Hartman, 27, has been with Washington since entering the league as an undrafted free gent in 2024. While he’s been on and off the 53-man roster, he has not yet appeared in a regular season game.

Hartman began his college career at Wake Forest before transferring to Notre Dame for his final season in 2023.

This is not the first time The Bachelor has chosen a reserve quarterback as its lead contestant. Way back in 2004, Jesse Palmer was with the Giants as the first professional athlete to appear on the program.

Palmer is now the host of the show.

item.title: Bruce Arians says he wants to be a head coach in the NFL next season
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Bruce Arians is thinking about coming out of retirement.
item.content:encoded:
Bruce Arians is thinking about coming out of retirement. Again.

Arians told Jordan Schultz that when he announced his retirement from the Buccaneers in March of 2022, it was because of health problems that have since been resolved, and he now wants to coach again.

"I had torn my Achilles early in that season, and I was wearing these prosthetic high heels, and it threw my back out, and I couldn't stand on the sideline for four hours anymore without a lot of pain," Arians said. "I was also monitoring an aneurysm on my heart, so I had some health issues. We did everything we thought we could do in Tampa after winning the Super Bowl, trying to get two, and then it was time to give it to Todd [Bowles]. Now that I'm all healthy again, I got the itch again. So, we'll see."

If Arians does come back next year, he'll be the oldest head coach in NFL history. That distinction currently belongs to Pete Carroll, who was 74 when he coached the Raiders last season. Arians will turn 75 next season.

Arians' first retirement announcement came from the Steelers after they did not renew his contract as their offensive coordinator following the 2011 season, but Arians later said he was forced out and didn't want to retire. He then took a job as offensive coordinator of the Colts in 2012, and was their interim head coach for most of that season while Chuck Pagano battled leukemia. Arians coached so well that he was named the NFL's Coach of the Year.

Once Pagano returned to the Colts, Arians became head coach of the Cardinals, and he won a second Coach of the Year award. He announced his retirement following the 2017 season, after five years as head coach of the Cardinals.

But in 2019 he came out of retirement to become head coach of the Buccaneers. He won a Super Bowl in Tampa Bay, then retired after three seasons. Arians thought that was it, but he said that his son is now coaching high school football, and in talking to his son about the job he realized how much he misses it himself.

"Another fire got lit," Arians said. "I had no desire to go back, and I was still fighting some health issues, but now after the open heart surgery I've got so much more energy, it's amazing."

Arians may find, like Bill Belichick before him, that all the accomplishments in the world don't guarantee an NFL head-coaching job. Or perhaps he'll convince some owner to give the oldest coach ever a chance to do what he's done three times before, and turn a franchise around.

item.title: DeMarvion Overshown didn't know inactive players couldn't celebrate on the field
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Cowboys had 14 accepted penalties for 153 yards in the 27-23 win over the Colts.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys had 14 accepted penalties for 153 yards in the 27-23 win over the Colts. One of them was called unacceptable and undisciplined by Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones.

Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who was inactive and dressed in street clothes, came onto the field to celebrate after Quinnen Williams forced a Jonathan Taylor fumble that Shemar James returned to the Dallas 30. Overshown was penalized 15 yards, with referee Clay Martin saying, "After the play, unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas. We have non-uniformed player in blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate. That's a 15-yard penalty."

Overshown apologized to head coach Brian Schottenheimer and his teammates.

“At the end of the day, I talked to Schotty about it," Overshown said Thursday, via Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News. "I apologized about it. It was definitely in the moment, but earlier I had said that as a defense, we're going to start celebrating more, getting takeaways. And I was just caught in the moment. So you can laugh at it now, because we won the game, but in the moment, fourth quarter, tied ball game or close ball game, you don't want a 15-yard penalty from a guy, especially that's not even playing. So that's a lesson learned.”

Overshown said he didn't know the rule until linebacker Dee Winters started yelling at him, which should prompt questions about why Overshown didn't know the rule. But he defended Schottenheimer and said he accepted his "butt chewing."

“It’s not an indictment on Schotty. It’s on me as a player. I own it,” he said.

item.title: Broncos have no comment as to Jim Harbaugh's complaints about Daiyan Henley trade
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The failed Daiyan Henley trade has exposed a previously unknown (by many) loophole in the trade deadline, which could be used by an unscrupulous team to leverage better terms after a deal is otherwise done — and the time for negotiating trades has otherwise ended.
item.content:encoded:
The failed Daiyan Henley trade has exposed a previously unknown (by many) loophole in the trade deadline, which could be used by an unscrupulous team to leverage better terms after a deal is otherwise done — and the time for negotiating trades has otherwise ended.

Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh essentially accused the Broncos of being unscrupulous by taking the position that Henley had failed his physical but that the physical would magically be un-failed if the compensation for Henley was reduced from a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick.

In response to an inquiry from PFT, the Broncos had no comment on the situation.

During a normal week, Broncos coach Sean Payton would be meeting with reporters on Friday. Because Denver has a Week 10 bye, Payton won't speak to the media again until Monday.

At that point, it will be interesting to see whether he shares the Broncos' position, or whether he makes it clear that Denver is moving on.

Of course, that doesn't stop the Broncos from pushing their position on an off-the-record basis to one of the reporters who routinely covers the team. And their position seems to be that the Broncos believe the Chargers weren't candid about the condition of Henley's knee during the discussions that preceded the trade.

The Broncos also contend, not on the record (yet), that the goal was to acquire Henley (who is in the last year of his contract) not as a rental but as a long-term addition. (They would have acquired exclusive negotiating rights with Henley through the opening of the legal tampering period in March.)

Still, with Harbaugh making his case on the record, the Broncos should do the same. While there's surely some sensitivity to the impact of the chatter about Henley's knee on his future earning potential, the options (in our view) should be to address the situation on the record or say nothing.

Through it all, the more important point is that the league's procedures allow things like this to happen. And, apparently, deadline deals have indeed been tweaked in the past based on concerns about a player's physical.

It shouldn't be that way. For any deal done before 4:00 p.m. ET on the day the trade window closes, there should be two possible outcomes: The player passes the physical and the deal goes through as negotiated, or the player fails the physical and the player reverts to his prior team.

item.title: Bengals designate Andrei Iosivas, two others for return from IR
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bengals will have three players back at practice on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals will have three players back at practice on Thursday.

They announced that they have designated wide receiver Andrei Iosivas, cornerback Jalen Davis, and guard Brian Parker for return from injured reserve. All three players will be able to practice with the team for the next 21 days and they can return to the active roster at any point in that window.

Iosivas has been out since Week 2 with a thumb injury. He had three catches for 19 yards in the first two weeks of the season and had 69 catches over the previous two seasons.

Davis played in the first three games and has been out with a hamstring injury. He had five tackles, a tackle for loss and a pass defensed before his injury.

Parker was a sixth-round pick this year and landed on injured reserve ahead of Week 1.

item.title: Failed Daiyan Henley trade exposes a flaw in the NFL's trade deadline
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The trade deadline is the trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
The trade deadline is the trade deadline. Except when it's not the trade deadline.

The strange situation involving the failed trade of Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Broncos reveals a major flaw in the NFL's deadline-day machinery.

Adam Schefter of ESPN has provided the details (which we have confirmed to be accurate) in the most nonchalant, innocuous terms possible: "It is not uncommon for one team to have some medical concerns about a player while another does not. In this case, Denver had concerns about Henley following his physical. Even then, the Broncos still wanted Henley with Denver and LA discussing revised trade alternatives throughout the day, taking into account those concerns. In the end, no agreement was reached. The deal was off."

Here's what it means. The Chargers and Broncos struck a deal for Henley and independently communicated the terms to the NFL before the trade deadline of 4:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10. Like all trades, the Henley deal was subject to the player passing a physical.

The Broncos discovered an issue with Henley's knee. It has, we're told, arthritis. (As one source with neither the Chargers nor the Broncos told PFT, most if not all starting linebackers in the NFL have some degree of arthritis in their knees.)

The NFL allows trade terms to be revised after the deadline, to an extent. Per a league spokesperson: "We would permit them to change the pick compensation. They would not be able to add a player or trade a different player."

Instead of concluding that the physical had been failed and canceling the deal (like the Ravens did with the trade for Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby in March), the Broncos were willing to proceed with revised terms. In other words, for something less than a fourth-round pick in 2027 and a fifth-round pick in 2028, they'd still do the deal.

That's not how it should work after the deadline. The window has closed. The deals are done, or they're not. After 4:00 p.m. ET on November 10, the only question left to answer is whether the player passes or fails the physical.

As one source explained it, deadline-day deals have gone through in the past with terms that were revised after the deadline.

Based on Schefter's reporting, that's what happened here. The Broncos had "medical concerns," but not enough to reject the player. The Broncos and Chargers discussed "revised trade alternatives" on Wednesday — the day after the window for doing trades ended.

The Chargers could have taken less in order to get the deal done. They chose not to do so. The fact that the rules allow trade terms to be renegotiated after the deadline opened the door for the Broncos to squeeze the Chargers.

The situation creates an opportunity for shenanigans. If, for example, Team A is preparing to trade a player to Team B at the deadline for a fourth-round pick and a sixth-round pick, Team C can swoop in and offer a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick. Then, when the physical is performed after the deadline, Team C can say, "Well, we have medical concerns. If we don't agree to reduce the package to a fourth-round pick and a sixth-round pick, we're going to fail the player on his physical."

That's not to say the Broncos did it deliberately. Obviously, however, they remained interested in Henley (who has started all eight games this year and has participated in 89 percent of the snaps) at something less than the agreed terms.

The point is that this little-known ability to extend the trading period by giving the acquiring team the ability to use the physical to leverage better terms shouldn't exist. When a deal is done at the deadline, the trade should either go through for the agreed terms or it shouldn't.

It opens the door to gamesmanship. The team that has traded the player has no alternatives. It can't trade the player to someone else. It either has to accept reduced terms or try to put the toothpaste back in the tube.

The Vikings, for example, could have tried to do that to the Raiders regarding quarterback Kirk Cousins. "Well, we found something in Kirk's leg that we don't like. We're not comfortable giving up a third-round pick. How about a fifth-round pick instead?"

What would the Raiders have done at that point? They'd already turned the page to Fernando Mendoza, and they spent Tuesday and Wednesday getting him ready to play.

The rule needs to change. The ability to revisit trade terms after the deadline has passed should be eliminated. Either the deal gets done as negotiated, or it doesn't.

Hovering over all of this is the subjectivity that can result in a team failing a player on a physical if it wants that outcome. It's an easy way out for a team that has buyer's remorse. (The Bengals, for example, could have determined that Eagles defensive end Arnold Ebiketie failed his physical, if the Bengals hadn't realized until after the trade terms were finalized that the Bengals would lose a 2027 third-round compensatory pick if the trade became official.)

At some point, it makes sense for the physicals not to be conducted by team doctors but by an independent, unaffiliated physician. But that's for another day. For now, the immediate problem that needs to be solved is the ability of teams to renegotiate trade terms after the trade deadline.

No one benefits from that, and unscrupulous teams could use it to their advantage.

item.title: Jesse Minter: Injuries like Lamar Jackson's typically take 6-10 weeks to heal
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: In an unusual move, the Ravens released a written statement from their head coach to update the quarterback's injury status.
item.content:encoded:
On Monday, Ravens coach Jesse Minter declined to address quarterback Lamar Jackson's injury status. In a highly unusual move, the Ravens released a statement from Minter on Friday that did address Jackson's status.

"Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8," Minter said in the statement the Ravens published on social media and the team's website. "Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return. We are committed to playing our best football over the the season. second half of the season."

It's unclear why the Ravens decided to release this statement, this way. NFL teams rarely announce injury news via a written statement from the head coach. Typically if there's something to update, the coach will say it at his regularly scheduled press conference, or the player himself will say how he's doing. In more complex cases, a written statement might come from the team's medical staff, but not the head coach.

Jackson suffered the injury in Week 8, which means that the 6-10 week timeline would but his return somewhere in the Week 14 to Week 18 neighborhood. Realistically, the Ravens may not be in playoff contention by the time Jackson is cleared to return, which means Jackson's 2026 season may be over.

item.title: Daniel Jones is "not happy" with Colts' roster purge
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Colts had a mini-fire sale in recent weeks, trading away four starters for future assets.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts had a mini-fire sale in recent weeks, trading away four starters for future assets.

Quarterback Daniel Jones, not surprisingly, isn't thrilled by the decision to send guard Quenton Nelson, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, receiver Keenan Allen, and receiver Josh Downs to other teams.

"I mean, honestly, you’re not you’re not happy to see it, right?" Jones said. "You're a player and you're going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So you're not happy to see a lot of those decisions, and — but like I said, it's outside of our control, and our job is to play, be prepared, and play well.  So, like I said, we got a lot of trust in the guys coming in to those spots, and we'll be ready to go."

It's a bad situation for the players who remain, since it will be harder for them to win with backups thrust into the lineup. But that's how it works whenever a non-contender admits its situation and trades players.

Those who remain have to keep going, trying to win games even if they get the impression that the front office doesn't really care.

And even though the Jets hold the Colts' first-round pick, a bad season for Indianapolis will result in a higher spot in every round. As the Colts embark on a rebuild, it's not crazy to think the front office hopes to sink as low in the standings as possible, since that will enhance the priority of the picks they have.

The Jets will welcome that, since they have the Colts' first-round pick. Thanks to the failed trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner.

item.title: Falcons announce two-year contract extension with C.J. Henderson
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Falcons cornerback C.J.
item.content:encoded:
Falcons cornerback C.J. Henderson has agreed to a new contract.

The Falcons announced today that Henderson has signed a two-year extension.

This is Henderson's second season on the Falcons, but last year he was mostly a practice squad player who was only active for four games. This year, Henderson has started the last six games at boundary corner after A.J. Terrell went on injured reserve, and Henderson has played very well in his place. Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich praised Henderson for how well he has played after being thrust into a new role.

"It's been a fun journey with C.J. because when he got here, obviously, he had a very well-known past in this league," Ulbrich said, via the Falcons' website. "To help him start to reinvent himself here, it brings me a ton of joy because he's just such an amazing young man. I'm excited for every opportunity he gets and every opportunity to show this league exactly who he is now, today."

The 28-year-old Henderson entered the NFL with the Jaguars as the ninth overall pick in the 2020 draft. He was a disappointment in Jacksonville and got traded to the Panthers during his second season, and for most of his NFL career he has been viewed as a draft bust. But he got a big opportunity in Atlanta when Terrell went down, and he's made the most of it. Now he's getting rewarded.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Stefon Diggs' late TD gives Commanders 24-21 win
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The wide receiver caught a 32-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels with 57 seconds left.
item.content:encoded:
With 3:27 remaining in Thursday's game, the Giants lined up with Jameis Winston under center on fourth-and-1 from their own 11. The team's backup quarterback, who runs the team's quarterback sneaks, yelled, "Hut One. Hut Two. Hut Three. Who let the dogs out? Who, who, who, who?"

The Giants took a delay of game and then punted.

The Commanders got the last laugh, winning 24-21 on Stefon Diggs' 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. The Commanders are 3-5-1 and the Giants 5-3-1.

In an entertaining second half, the teams traded the lead four times.

The Giants took a 21-17 lead with 8:13 left on Isaiah Likely's 66-yard catch-and-run.

The Giants then had back-to-back interceptions of Jayden Daniels. Safety Jevon Holland, who is having an All-Pro season, took the ball away from Chig Okonkwo at the 2-yard line with the Commanders on the Giants 24 with 5:27 left, and Ar'Darius Washington stepped in front of Okonkwo on fourth-and-2 at the Washington 45 with 2:15 left.

The Giants, though, couldn't run out the clock, and the Commanders made the most of it. They needed only three plays to go 71 yards thanks to a questionable 33-yard pass interference penalty on Deonte Banks, who was covering Treylon Burks. Three plays later, Diggs scored.

The Giants reached the Washington 48 on their final drive, but J.J. McCarthy's deep throw to Malik Nabers was intercepted by Rasul Douglas with 25 seconds left to end it.

The Giants outgained the Commanders 399 to 340, but missed a field goal and had two turnovers.

Daniels was 23-of-33 for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions. Rachaad White ran for 47 yards on 11 carries, and Diggs caught six passes for 83 yards. Antonio Williams and Ben Sinnott each caught a touchdown pass.

McCarthy was 23-of-36 for 293 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Cam Skattebo had 18 carries for 78 yards and two touchdowns and caught three passes for 44 yards, and Likely had nine receptions for 127 yards and a touchdown.

item.title: Falcons extend Cameron Thomas through 2029
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: In March, free agent defensive end Cameron Thomas signed a one-year, $3.1 million contract with the Falcons.
item.content:encoded:
In March, free agent defensive end Cameron Thomas signed a one-year, $3.1 million contract with the Falcons. He has played well enough that the Falcons are keeping him around, and paying him a lot more money.

Thomas and the Falcons have reached an agreement on a three-year contract extension through the 2029 season, according to ESPN. The report says the deal is worth "up to" $33 million, which generally means he won't actually make $11 million a year, but will make a lot more than $3.1 million a year.

Originally a third-round pick of the Cardinals in 2022, but was traded to the Chiefs after two years, was waived by the Chiefs and then claimed by the Browns. He was never a major impact player in any of his previous NFL stops, but this year he has started every game for the Falcons.

Now the Falcons expect Thomas to be a starter for years to come.

item.title: Buccaneers have more rushing yards than passing yards, a rare feat in today's NFL
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: With the 2026 NFL season at the midway point, one of the bigger statistical oddities belongs to the Buccaneers, who are the only team in the league with more rushing yards than passing yards.
item.content:encoded:
With the 2026 NFL season at the midway point, one of the bigger statistical oddities belongs to the Buccaneers, who are the only team in the league with more rushing yards than passing yards.

Through nine games, the Buccaneers have 1,475 rushing yards and 1,277 passing yards. Every other team has gained more yardage passing than running, and no other team is even close to having more rushing than passing yards.

The last time an NFL team finished a season with more rushing yards than passing yards was 2022, when the Bears finished with an NFL-high 3,014 rushing yards and an NFL-low 2,219 passing yards. That Bears team was led by Justin Fields, who rushed for 1,143 yards himself, but netted just 1,883 passing yards. With running back David Montgomery chipping in 801 rushing yards and Khalil Herbert gaining 731, the Bears were a team that could run effectively but couldn't pass for anything.

The Buccaneers' yardage totals come from some fairly unique circumstances. Baker Mayfield has played some of the worst football of his career when healthy, and he was also injured and missed three games, replaced by undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. That has led the Bucs to rely more on their running game. And the weather contributed a huge portion of the Buccaneers' run-pass yardage differential in Week 8, when the Bucs gained 322 yards rushing and minus-2 yards passing in a downpour against the Falcons.

Despite their one-dimensional offense, the Buccaneers are still playoff contenders, thanks to the NFC South's status as the worst division in football. It won't be surprising if there's a playoff game in Tampa in January. If that happens, Bucs fans may be praying for another downpour.

item.title: Luke McCaffrey knew the rules and made a heads-up play, causing a kickoff out of bounds
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Commanders kickoff returner Luke McCaffrey made the smartest play of the game by not returning a kick in Thursday night's win over the Giants.
item.content:encoded:
Commanders kickoff returner Luke McCaffrey made the smartest play of the game by not returning a kick in Thursday night's win over the Giants.

With McCaffrey back to field a Giants kickoff, the ball landed near the sideline at the 5-yard line. The kick stayed in bounds, and some returners would have grabbed the ball and started running. But McCaffrey let the ball bounce, then stepped out of bounds, and then grabbed the ball with his feet down on the sideline.

By rule, the ball is out of bounds if it touches a player who is out of bounds, even if the ball actually stays in bounds. By touching the ball while his feet were out of bounds, McCaffrey forced a kickoff out of bounds penalty on the Giants, putting the ball on the 40-yard line for the Commanders.

"I thought Luke McCaffrey made a really smart play that won't show up on the stat sheet," Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said. "That's a difficult play. Is it out of bounds? Is it not? I was nervous about it, that's one of the ones where you hold your breath."

Every kickoff returner needs to know that rule, but knowing the rule is easier than having the quick-thinking ability to do what McCaffrey did, in the fourth quarter with the game on the line. It was among the smartest football plays you'll see.

item.title: Dan Quinn: We needed that, we needed every bit of it
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: After the win, the Commanders are 3-5-1, two games behind the division-leading Giants.
item.content:encoded:
The Commanders headed into Thursday night's game against the Giants desperately needing to win, if they wanted to have any chance of competing in the NFC East. After their 24-21 win, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn was a combination of exuberant and relieved.

"We needed that. We needed every bit of it," Quinn said. "This is one we had to have, and our guys make sure we have it."

After the win, the Commanders are 3-5-1, two games behind the division-leading Giants, and the Commanders now own the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Giants. Quinn's team is still a long shot to win the NFC East, but given the state of that division, it's not unreasonable to think the Commanders can compete.

And compete is what they did on Thursday night, in a game that went down to the final minute, just as Quinn said the Commanders expected.

"Going into it, we thought this is going to be all four quarters," Quinn said. "It felt like the most adversity, but also the most belief. It was a balance of both, and we definitely needed that."

item.title: John Harbaugh expresses confidence in K Dominic Zvada
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Giants rookie kicker Dominic Zvada has missed six field goals in nine games.
item.content:encoded:
Giants rookie kicker Dominic Zvada has missed six field goals in nine games. He missed another on Thursday night, a 33-yarder.

While it happened in the first quarter and not on the final play, it stands out in a game that was decided by three points.

After New York's 24-21 loss to the Commanders, Giants coach John Harbaugh was asked about his level of confidence in Zvada.

"Yeah, we’re confident," Harbaugh said. "You know, you can't — as soon as a guy doesn't make a play, I mean, start firing people left and right. Especially your kicker who's a rookie. So I'm confident that he's gonna become a good kicker. I mean, if at some point in time, it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen.

"But I'm not gonna panic, you know, halfway through the season when the guy who's made a bunch of kicks, if that's what you're inferring we should be doing.  So, you know, I mean, we're just not gonna knee-jerk it like that. He's gonna make kicks. He's gonna make a lot of kicks, I believe in him.  I think he's really good, really talented. And we're gonna give him an opportunity to do it. It's up to him to do it."

That's a fair assessment of a player who's still new to the NFL. But a kicker has one job. If he can't do it (especially from distances that should be automatic), at some point tough questions need to be asked.

Basically, how much time will Zvada get before Harbaugh decides it's not going to happen? That remains to be seen, if Zvada keeps missing kicks he should be making.

item.title: Aaron Donald on having no sacks: "They come in bunches"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald has played seven games this season.
item.content:encoded:
Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald has played seven games this season. He has no sacks.

“Sacks come in bunches," Donald told reporters on Thursday. "It's going to come. Just keep playing ball and keep finding ways to win. That's the most important thing is winning. No pressure, I'm not worried about it. I've been playing football since I was five, six years old. They come in bunches. They'll come eventually so just keep doing what I need to do to help this team. When they present themselves, hopefully hold the ball and take advantage of it.”

On Sunday, Donald finally played with Myles Garrett, the player whose arrival in June sparked Donald's decision to return after two years of retirement. Garrett, in his first game since Week 1, had 3.0 sacks and a forced fumble.

Regardless, the Rams won, pushing themselves above .500 for the first time this year. On Sunday at Arizona, they have a chance to win their fourth in a row.

And Donald has another chance to get his first sack since he returned from retirement.

item.title: Report: Rex Ryan incident was captured on camera
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The recent news that Rex Ryan, of all people, allegedly ran over, of all the things, the feet of a pair of pedestrians in Nashville seems too crazy to be true, absent visual evidence.
item.content:encoded:
The recent news that Rex Ryan, of all people, allegedly ran over, of all the things, the feet of a pair of pedestrians in Nashville seems too crazy to be true, absent visual evidence.

Apparently, there is visual evidence.

Via TMZ.com, the incident "was captured on camera." The video has not yet surfaced, but it presumably will at some point.

Ryan was arrested on six misdemeanor charges arising from the allegation that he ran over the feet of two people while driving a pickup truck on November 12.

ESPN hasn't said much about the situation. From a one-line statement issued on Wednesday: “We are aware and are in touch with Rex."

It's unclear whether he'll appear on Sunday morning's ESPN pregame show, or whether he'll make any appearances while the criminal case is pending.

Ryan, who coached the Jets and the Bills before pivoting to TV, is scheduled to appear in court next month.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Commanders lead Giants 10-7 at halftime
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Ben Sinnott caught a 1-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels with 5 seconds remaining in the first half.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants and Commanders played a first half fitting the weather. On a cold, rainy night, the Commanders lead the Giants 10-7 at halftime.

Ben Sinnott caught a 1-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels with 5 seconds remaining in the first half. It completed a nine-play, 67-yard drive.

Washington also had an 11-play, 49-yard drive that ended with Drew Stevens' 46-yard field goal.

Daniels was 11-of-15 for 112 yards and a touchdown in the first half. Rachaad White had six carries for 20 yards, and Stefon Diggs caught two passes for 34 yards.

The Giants outgained the Commanders 152 to 143 and had 12 first downs and a 17:18 to 12:42 advantage in time of possession.

Cam Skattebo ran for a 1-yard touchdown with 2:35 remaining in the second quarter, giving New York its first lead at 7-3. It capped a 16-play, 72-yard drive.

The Giants punted after reaching the Washington 37 on their first drive, and Dominic Zvada missed a 33-yard field goal after the Giants stalled at the Washington 15 on the second drive.

Skattebo had 35 yards and a touchdown on eight carries and two catches for 37 yards. J.J. McCarthy went 12-of-19 for 92 yards and rushed for 30 yards on four carries. Isaiah Likely had five catches for 39 yards.

Commanders tight end Chig Okonkwo (back) is questionable to return.
